page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a virtual machine instance from the Lasv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, offering 960 GB of Premium Storage capable capacity. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is average, and memory bandwidth presents a notable bottleneck, with both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%. This memory limitation is reflected in weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation benchmarks. Database operations also show weaker performance, with Passmark database operations scoring in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and bundled local storage, the L4as_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extreme multi-threaded throughput or high-speed memory reads. It is suitable for memory-optimized applications, single-threaded processing tasks, static web serving, and lightweight text processing. It is less suited for heavy database operations, complex software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference due to memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling constraints.
